The success of completing the Perinatal Education Programme (PEP) is not necessarily linked to improved obstetric practice. While the programme aimed to enhance midwives' knowledge, a recent study found that completion of the PEP did not lead to any changes in obstetric practices.

According to the completed match, "Completion of the obstetric manual of the PEP improved the knowledge of the midwives but no alteration in practice was detected." This suggests that while the programme's goal of improving midwives' understanding may have had an impact on their knowledge, it did not directly lead to changes in obstetric practices.

In other words, completing the PEP program likely contributed to better understanding and communication among healthcare providers regarding perinatal care, but these efforts did not translate into significant improvements in clinical practice.
